episode.title: How Tree Rings Proved Vikings Reached America In 1021!

synopsis: Scientific analysis of tree rings, marked by a solar storm, precisely dated the Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows to 1021 AD.
narration: Tree rings, marked by a powerful solar storm, precisely dated the Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows. This cosmic event left a distinct signal, allowing scientists to confirm that Norse explorers were present in Newfoundland exactly in 1021 AD.

shots.prompt: A close-up, dramatic shot of a cross-section of ancient, petrified wood. A gloved archaeologist's hand with a magnifying glass points to a specific, unusually thick tree ring. The wood grain is intricate and detailed.

A wide, establishing shot of a reconstructed sod-roofed Viking longhouse nestled on a windswept, grassy coastal bluff in Newfoundland. A few period-accurate Norse settlers work near the entrance, under a dramatic, cloudy sky.

music: A mysterious, driving score with a deep, resonant percussive pulse and sweeping, ancient-sounding string motifs. It evokes both the vastness of the ocean and the precision of scientific discovery, building with a sense of revelation and historical weight, ending mid-phrase.
